issue.title: Land bead close integrity — unblock the core release and finish the repair
issue.description: The declared `sase-core-rs` floor names a published release that actually contains `note_appended` and `bead_doctor_report`, so an ordinary install can read the live bead store and the `published-core-minimum-smoke` CI lane is green; the beads still carrying dropped note revisions are either restored or explicitly declined by the user, with the decision recorded; and epic `sase-bd` is closed with its plan file marked done.

issue.title: Unblock sase-core master
issue.description: core-clippy: fix the `clippy::question_mark` denial in the doctor reader that has kept sase-core master red since the projection-drift commit, sweep the neighbouring commits for the same class of denial, and confirm master CI goes green so release-plz can cut a release.

issue.title: Publish the release containing all four core commits
issue.description: core-release: merge the refreshed release PR once master is green, then confirm the published wheel is actually installable from the package index and carry the real published version forward.

issue.title: Make the declared core floor honest
issue.description: floor-bump: raise the `sase-core-rs` window to the newly published release, refresh the lockfile and the declared-minimum test, and prove in a clean venv that the minimum satisfies every required binding and can read a store containing note-append events.

issue.title: Put the lost-note restore to the user
issue.description: lost-notes: re-measure the beads carrying dropped note revisions, present the restore to the user through an approval gate, run or decline it accordingly, and record the decision durably so it stops being absent.

issue.title: Close the epic
issue.description: land: close the epic bead with a note covering what was verified, run symvision and clear anything stale it reports, and mark the original plan file done.

payload.entry: Fixed the clippy::question_mark denial at crates/sase_core/src/bead/read.rs:232 by collapsing the match on read_legacy_jsonl_issues into the ? form. Swept the workspace rather than stopping at the first reported error, which surfaced a second denial hidden behind it (clippy stops at the first error per crate): a needless_borrow at crates/sase_core/tests/bead_read_parity.rs:594 passing &stream where stream was already a reference. Verified with the exact commands core CI runs: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace fully green (all suites, 0 failures; PYO3_PYTHON and LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointed at a 3.12 interpreter for the local pyo3 build). Committed and pushed to sase-core master as 407965e 'fix(bead): satisfy clippy in the doctor reader'. Master CI run 30578914929 for that commit concluded success with both jobs green: 'cargo fmt + clippy + test' and 'maturin build + import smoke'. Core master is no longer red, so release-plz can cut a release; PR #63 'chore: release v0.15.0' remains open for the core-release phase.

Merged sase-core release PR #63 (chore: release v0.15.0) after master went green on 407965e. Verified before merging that the refreshed release branch contained all four target commits (160ff9e, 293ccb2, 81a82d5, 6468cb9) plus the clippy fix, that all PR checks passed (cargo fmt+clippy+test, maturin build+import smoke), and that the proposed bump was a breaking 0.14.2 -> 0.15.0. Post-merge: master CI run 30580458464 green, Release-plz run 30580460440 green through 'publish to PyPI', tag v0.15.0 -> 803ff81 (the merge commit). Confirmed publication from the index, not the repo: 'uv pip install --no-cache sase-core-rs==0.15.0' into a clean 3.12 venv succeeded, tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings exited 0 ('exposes all 230 bindings required'), bead_doctor_report is present, and bead_show against the live beads sidecar returned sase-bd.3 instead of raising 'unknown variant note_appended'. Published version to carry into floor-bump: 0.15.0. No repo file changes in this phase.

Updated pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and the declared-minimum telemetry test to carry published sase-core-rs 0.15.0 with range >=0.15.0,<0.16.0. Verified in a fresh Python 3.12 venv with only sase-core-rs==0.15.0 from PyPI: tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings reports all 230 bindings present, tools/smoke_sase_core_rs_telemetry passes, and sase_core_rs.bead_show reads live beads sidecar entry sase-bd.3 from a store containing note_appended events. Also verified python3 tools/smoke_sase_core_rs_telemetry --print-minimum pyproject.toml prints 0.15.0, .venv/bin/python tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version --pyproject pyproject.toml --published-minimum exits 0, focused pytest tests/test_sase_core_rs_telemetry_smoke_tool.py passes, and just install passes. Full just check passed fmt/lint through symvision/toobig, then failed only in final SASE validation on unrelated existing issues: init skills --check wants 5 provider skill overwrites and plan links validate reports 202607/prompts/commit_vars_finalizer.md missing ../commit_vars_finalizer.md.

Land phase done. (1) Recorded the full verification note on epic sase-bd; the close itself is blocked by the descendant guard (sase-bd.9 still in_progress) and I was instructed not to close my parent epic, so sase-bd closes once sase-bd.9 does. (2) 'just symvision' is clean -- 'All public/private classes/functions are used properly!' -- and the only --epic-symbol entries are sase-bf(coerce_var_value)/sase-bf(decode_var_value); no stale sase-bd whitelist entries exist, confirming the expected no-op. (3) plans:202607/bead_close_integrity.md frontmatter set to status: done (uncommitted in the plans sidecar). Verified independently: 'sase bead doctor' reports no projection drift and the unchanged census of 450 redundant close events across 312 beads (2 in last 7 days); sase-b8.8 projects closed_at 2026-07-30T16:10:17Z, its first close; 'sase bead history --lost-notes' reports none after beads commit 44648af restored 393 revisions; tools/smoke_sase_core_rs_telemetry --print-minimum prints 0.16.0 and a clean 3.12 venv with only sase-core-rs==0.16.0 passes check_sase_core_rs_bindings (230/230), passes the telemetry smoke, and reads the live beads sidecar without the note_appended serde error. No sase-repo files changed, so 'just check' was not required.

Backfilled by the sase-bd.9 land agent: this phase closed with no note, so its record was silent about what happened. Actual sequence: the phase agent measured 301 beads / 393 dropped note revisions, raised approval gate custom-69fcbb88-1a72-4c3e-b8f0-6393c0c29fac (approve path = 'sase bead history --lost-notes --restore --yes', decline path = no-op), waited, and stopped still blocked without running the restore or writing any note. The user approved the gate afterwards; the gate executor ran the restore as beads commit 44648af (393 revisions, events/streams/*.jsonl only). The phase's remaining 'done when' -- recording the outcome on sase-bd.8 -- was never met; the land agent has now written that note on sase-bd.8. Verified: 'sase bead history --lost-notes' reports none and 'sase bead doctor' shows no projection drift.

Land verification for sase-bd.9. VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE AND THE LIVE STORE, not agent self-reports. (1) core-clippy: commit 407965e is real in sase-core; crates/sase_core/src/bead/read.rs:232 now uses the '?' form and the hidden needless_borrow in the parity test is gone; sase-core master CI has been green since. (2) core-release: tag v0.15.0 -> 803ff81 exists and carries 160ff9e, 293ccb2, 81a82d5 and 6468cb9; v0.16.0 has since shipped on top of it. (3) floor-bump: the epic set >=0.15.0,<0.16.0 in f115e8f7a; a later unrelated epic (sase-bf, commit 2b95bd329) raised it to >=0.16.0,<0.17.0 and updated tests/test_sase_core_rs_telemetry_smoke_tool.py and uv.lock (locked 0.16.0) consistently, so the floor stayed honest and got stronger rather than regressing. The real acceptance test is independently green: CI job 'published-core-minimum-smoke' on master HEAD 668bf209d passed, meaning the exact declared minimum installed from PyPI with no source checkout or override exposes every required binding including bead_doctor_report. Core source confirms NoteAppended (events.rs:119/141) and first-close preservation (events.rs:755-757 only stamps closed_at when not already closed), and bead_doctor_report is exported at crates/sase_core_py/src/lib.rs:3496. (4) lost-notes: the restore genuinely ran under real user approval -- the phase agent raised gate custom-69fcbb88-1a72-4c3e-b8f0-6393c0c29fac and stopped without mutating anything while it was pending; the user approved it afterwards and the executor produced beads commit 44648af restoring 393 revisions across events/streams only. 'sase bead history --lost-notes' now reports none and 'sase bead doctor' shows no projection drift with the census unchanged at 450 redundant closes across 312 beads. GAP FOUND AND FIXED: the phase's own 'done when' -- record the outcome on sase-bd.8 -- was never met (sase-bd.9.4 closed with no note at all, the exact failure mode this epic exists to correct). I wrote that note on sase-bd.8 and backfilled an honest note on sase-bd.9.4. sase-b8.8 still projects its first close, 2026-07-30T16:10:17Z. (5) INTEGRATION: reviewed all nine commits landed since this epic started (84d47aa78..668bf209d). Only two touch this epic's surface: 2b95bd329 (floor bump, integrates correctly as above) and 3b6f58960 (refactor(cli): split bead parser registrations), which preserved every flag this epic depends on -- --force in parser_bead_lifecycle.py:35, --lost-notes/--restore/--yes in parser_bead_queries.py:58-72 -- with the honest close-outcome rows (Closed / Already closed / Noted) intact in cli_crud.py:234-258 and doctor repair still routed through core. No duplication or conflict found, and no stale references to the old 0.14.2/0.15.0 floor remain anywhere in src/, tools/, tests/, docs/ or .github/. NOT MINE, REPORTED NOT FIXED: 'just lint' fails on two stale --epic-symbol entries at Justfile:273-274 for the now-closed sase-bf epic (coerce_var_value, decode_var_value have no src/ callers); master also has an unrelated ACE TUI test failure and two SDD plan-link errors in the plans sidecar. All belong to sase-bf's landing, not to this epic; I did not delete another epic's just-shipped code.
